question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only two people sit between C and G when counted from the left of G. A sits third to the left of D. E sits to the immediate right of D. E sits second to the left of C. B is an immediate neighbour of A. How many people sit between B and E when counted from the right of B?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

 
• Only two people sit between C and G when counted from the left of G.
 
• A sits third to the left of D.
 
• E sits to the immediate right of D.
 
• E sits second to the left of C.
 
• B is an immediate neighbour of A
